newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-INJURIES HIT WELSH BEFORE ITALY TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-INJURIES HIT WELSH BEFORE ITALY TEST.

text.p: Wales will be forced to name a reshuffled back division for their match against Italy in Rome on October 5 after injuries to record try-scorer Ieuan Evans and stand-in captain Nigel Davies.

Evans took his tally of Welsh test tries to 28 in the 40-33 defeat by France, but suffered a gashed thigh preventing opposite number Philippe Saint-Andre from scoring and will definitely miss the Italy match.

Davies, also stretchered off in the first half, was taken to hospital for X-rays on an ankle injury and is expected to be unavailable too, leaving Wales with a selection headache before they announce their team on Friday.
Regular captain and hooker Jonathan Humphreys is hoping to return after a hamstring injury, but saw his replacement Barry Williams mark his Welsh debut with a try inside the first two minutes.
"We're a bit battered and bruised," said Welsh coach Kevin Bowring, disappointed his side had allowed a 27-10 half-time lead to slip.
"We defended our lead rather than going for the jugular. There were a few off-the-ball incidents but we expect that from the French."

French captain Jean-Claude Skrela criticised his team for a lack of control in the first half and agreed some of his players, notably centre Richard Dourthe and lock Olivier Merle, had been guilty of a lack of discipline.
"I saw only two or three incidents, but they happened on both sides. They were not pleasant and I disapprove," he said.
